comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount kept, not widened, in the base case. Persistent factors with evidence: (1) wildfire liability without a state shield in Colorado (2025 bill to cap utility liability dropped) and Texas (AG suit seeking damages and civil penalties), after $640M Marshall and ~$503M Smokehouse losses; (2) Moody's negative outlook at the holdco (Baa1) and PSCo (A1), with planned FFO/debt flat at ~16% through 2028; (3) EPS growth more equity-funded than peers ($7B base equity, 69.7M forward shares unsettled), so per-share growth lags rate-base growth; (4) Colorado regulatory friction (9.3% ROE vs 9.8% asked; consumer advocate calling it the largest increase in state history). Higher rate-base growth (11%) argues against a wider discount, so we do not go below the current level in the base case.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$64 (about -17%, under the 52-week low of $68.72 and roughly 1.0 sigma of annual vol) the market would be pricing NTM EPS near $4.30 at ~15x or a de-rating to ~13.7x (ES-like): most likely a new utility-caused wildfire with liability above insurance in CO/TX, a Moody's holdco downgrade, an equity-heavy capex plan that cuts EPS growth to ~6%, or a regulatory reversal (e.g. ROE <9% in CO), rather than ordinary rate-driven volatility.

reverse_dcf_check: Engine reverse DCF: the 17.0x P/E leg ($79) implies a WACC of 5.5% with 3.5% terminal growth, i.e. a cost of equity of ~6.7% against a 5.1% 10-year Treasury (an equity risk premium of only ~1.6pt) - or, at our 6.2% WACC, perpetual growth well above 3.5% / earned returns above allowed. Plausible only if (a) long rates fall back toward 4-4.5%, or (b) the data-center pipeline keeps rate base compounding ~8-10% well past 2030 with ROE above the cost of equity. The post-horizon risks (wildfire without a liability cap, ROE compression from affordability pushback, AI-capex slowdown) cut against (b); this is why we do not pay the peer-median multiple and why the blended fair value ($70.93) sits below the price.
dcf_check: The engine DCF ($38.48/share) is 51% below the P/E leg ($79.04). Not a modelling error but the bear point in numbers: with the 10y UST at 5.1% the cost of equity (~8%) is close to allowed ROEs (9.2%-9.6%) and the effective earned return (~8.9%) is below allowed, so growth capex adds little NPV, while ~$40B of 2026-2029 capex is funded before it earns and the holdco carries 22-25% of group debt, so equity is a thin, levered slice of EV (about $8-10/share per 0.2pt of WACC). The regulated-equity identity (rate base x equity ratio x ROE/COE less holdco debt) gives ~$49, corroborating the DCF side. The engine's reverse DCF says the P/E leg needs a 5.5% WACC (cost of equity ~6.7% with 10y at 5.1%). Kept at the band weight 0.2, not zeroed.

reasoning: Research (skeptic lane): read the Q2 2026 8-K and deck, fact pack, credit ratings, wildfire disclosures, Texas AG suit, Colorado rate-case opposition, MN large-load tariff, insider Form 4 data, consensus and the 10y yield. Bear evidence: (1) rates - 10y UST 5.09% vs 3.99% a year ago, the main reason a bond-proxy utility with 9% growth has de-rated to 17.2x NTM vs a peer median of 18.85x; (2) credit - Moody's negative outlook at holdco (Baa1) and PSCo (A1), planned FFO/debt flat at ~16%, holdco debt 22-25% of total; (3) dilution - $7B base equity, 69.7M forward shares unsettled (11% of outstanding), +40% equity on any incremental capex, so per-share growth lags 11% rate-base growth; (4) wildfire - Marshall $640M settled, Smokehouse estimate up from $215M to $430M to $503M with only ~$80M of insurance left, Texas AG suit seeking damages and civil penalties, no Colorado liability shield; (5) regulation - PSCo awarded 9.3% vs 9.8% asked, consumer advocate calls it the largest increase in Colorado history, rider-driven bills +22% in three years. Mitigants: constructive MN outcome (ROE 9.25%->9.6%), Google ESA where Google pays all costs, MN large-load tariff (15-year minimum, 80% exit demand charge) putting AI-tenant counterparty risk on the customer rather than shareholders, guidance reaffirmed, insiders only routine sales (EVP 15,969 sh at $83.61 in March, no open-market buys; not a signal). Valuation: rate-base EPS build gives FY27 $4.42 / FY28 $4.72 (2-4% below consensus/guide path because of dilution and ~0.6pt regulatory lag), NTM $4.66 x 17.0x = $79; DCF $38.5 at a 6.2% WACC; blend at band weights $70.93. Anthropic/WSJ: no verified Anthropic link to Xcel's territory (Google, Anthropic's largest compute partner at $111B of commitments per WSJ, has a signed MN ESA, but no source ties that site to Anthropic); the S-1's ~$450B-$750B compute commitments are a positive general demand signal for the ~4 GW Xcel expects to sign by 2027, but Anthropic's own risk factor that data-center opposition is 'more organized and coordinated' fits the affordability fight in Colorado; counterparty risk sits mostly on tariff minimum terms. A large IPO could pull flows from AI-adjacent names, but XEL trades as a rate-sensitive utility, so that is a second-order effect next to the 10y. Distribution: scenarios $62 (27%) / $77.5 (50%) / $90 (23%) with 11-12% within-scenario vol; median ~$76.4 (about spot; price beats blends as a forecast), mean ~$76.7, a skeptic tilt in the left tail. Research limits: Bigdata.com search was out of credits, several press sites blocked fetches (CPR 403), and Moody's rationale for the negative outlook was not found.

model_inputs.structure_note: Regulated utility: value carried by a P/E leg (weight 0.8) on our own rate-base EPS build (avg rate base x 53.5% equity ratio x 8.9% effective earned ROE incl. AFUDC, less holdco interest, over a diluted share count that includes the 69.7M unsettled forward shares), and a driver DCF (weight 0.2 per the forward-P/E band: 76.68 / FY2027 consensus $4.54 = 16.9x -> 0.20). The engine's EBIT is an 'economic EBIT' = operating income + AFUDC/other income, with tax credits netted (tax_rate 0, cash taxes ~nil because PTC/ITC are transferred; reported tax was a benefit of $245M on $1,773M pretax in FY2025, F71/F78), calibrated so EBIT - interest reproduces the build's net income (FY2026 $4,296M - $1,716M = $2,580M ~ guidance midpoint x shares; FY2027 $4,938M - $1,936M = $3,002M ~ build $2,997M). FY2030 capex is set to the steady-state reinvestment (D&A + 3.5% x $94B rate base + ~$0.5B AFUDC) so the Gordon terminal is internally consistent; plan capex above that is assumed NPV-neutral (allowed ROE ~ cost of equity).
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value is the engine's base horizon value for this set (no scenario deltas). The engine's own NTM EPS ((NOPAT - interest on horizon net debt) / horizon shares) reads ~$4.94 because it uses year-end-like 700M shares and $44.7B net debt rather than NTM averages (~712M, ~$47B); on averages it is $4.64, within 1% of the $4.66 build, which is why the P/E leg takes the stated EPS.
model_inputs.dcf_check: The engine DCF ($38.48/share) is 51% below the P/E leg ($79.04). Not a modelling error but the bear point in numbers: with the 10y UST at 5.1% the cost of equity (~8%) is close to allowed ROEs (9.2%-9.6%) and the effective earned return (~8.9%) is below allowed, so growth capex adds little NPV, while ~$40B of 2026-2029 capex is funded before it earns and the holdco carries 22-25% of group debt, so equity is a thin, levered slice of EV (about $8-10/share per 0.2pt of WACC). The regulated-equity identity (rate base x equity ratio x ROE/COE less holdco debt) gives ~$49, corroborating the DCF side. The engine's reverse DCF says the P/E leg needs a 5.5% WACC (cost of equity ~6.7% with 10y at 5.1%). Kept at the band weight 0.2, not zeroed.
